jobs.title: Revenue Operations Lead
jobs.jd_full:
The Role We Need

PadSplit's demand engine spans Marketing, Lifecycle, Member Acquisition, and Member Success, but no one owns how these teams connect once a lead is approved, leaving us blind to where members stall on the way to a move-in and unable to see which outreach actually converts. We need a Revenue Operations Lead to own the last, most critical leg of the funnel: the calling and human outreach that turns an approved lead into a housed member, along with the reporting that makes the whole funnel legible. This role starts narrow (conversion and outreach) with room to expand into the broader Demand Growth function over time.

The Person We Are Looking For

We're looking for a builder-operator with 5+ years in revenue operations, growth operations, or funnel analytics, who is fluent in SQL or a BI tool like Hex, Mode, or Looker and has real instinct for calling operations, script testing, and agent coaching. This person uses AI daily to build reporting, analyze calls, and scale outreach, and has a clear point of view on where AI makes an ops team faster. They can hold many channels at once without losing the thread, and translate a messy funnel into decisions leadership can act on.

Here's What You'll Be Doing Day-to-Day:

  • Optimizing call performance: Own how members convert across AI-driven calls and human phone calls, refining scripts, follow-up cadence, and objection handling.
  • Coaching agents: Test what actually moves conversion and feed findings back to human agents and the teams they support.
  • Sequencing hand-offs: Decide where AI calls hand off to a person and where a person hands off to Lifecycle.
  • Building funnel dashboards: Maintain the end-to-end view of the demand funnel — lead to approved to booked to moved-in — primarily in Hex.
  • Closing reporting gaps: Surface stage-by-stage conversion, drop-off, and velocity without re-deriving data each time.
  • Driving retention outreach: Partner with Member Success to flag churn-risk changes and behavioral events, and proactively reach out before a member decides to leave.
  • Standing up interventions: Launch retention and transfer offers as caller campaigns or lifecycle text messages.
  • Fixing the stack: Bring order to lead routing, CRM hygiene, and experiment instrumentation, and set clear SLAs across Performance Marketing, Lifecycle, MA, and Member Success.

Here's What You'll Need to Be Successful:

  • RevOps background: 5+ years in revenue operations, sales operations, growth operations, or funnel analytics, ideally in a marketplace, subscription, or high-volume consumer-sales environment.
  • AI fluency: A strong AI toolkit used daily to build reporting, analyze calls, draft and test scripts, and scale outreach.
  • Analytical rigor: Fluency in SQL or a BI tool such as Hex, Mode, or Looker, with comfort tying operational work to conversion, velocity, and cost.
  • Funnel instinct: Real operating experience with lead routing, calling operations, script and cadence testing, and agent coaching.
  • Cross-team coordination: Ability to hold many channels at once — from AI callers to affiliates to market launch — without losing the thread.
  • Strong communication: Excellent English communication skills to work daily with US-based teams and partners.
  • Marketplace experience (bonus): Background in marketplace, proptech, real estate, or two-sided consumer platforms.
  • Zero-to-one experience (bonus): Track record standing up a RevOps or sales-ops function from scratch, including instrumentation and cross-team SLAs.

The Interview Process:

  • Your application will be reviewed for possible next steps by a human being in the PeopleOps department.
  • If you meet eligibility requirements, the next step would be a video call with a member of the PeopleOps team for about thirty (30) minutes.
  • If warranted, the next step would be a video interview with our VP of Member Growth for forty-five (45) minutes.
  • If warranted, the final step would be a video panel interview with additional stakeholders for one (1) hour. For this interview, a candidate would participate in a campaign exercise to the panel for discussion.
  • If warranted, then we move to contract!

Compensation

Compensation is based on the role's scope, national market benchmarks, the person's expertise and experience, and the impact of their contributions to our business goals.

Additional Information

Please note: Although the job posting says it's in Brazil, this is a fully remote position open to anyone in South America. This is a result of our Applicant Tracking System requiring a location to post the role on LinkedIn.

Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

Our Impact

Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that.
Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts.

About the Role:

    We're hiring a Lead Product Analyst, AI Products to be the analytics owner and measurement lead for HighLevel's AI pillar -Voice AI, Conversation AI, AI Employee, and Ask AI. These products are shipping fast with limited analytics foundation underneath them; we would provide value by creating consistent instrumentation, agreed success metrics, and a rigorous read on adoption or quality. You'll build that from the ground up.

    Your first job is to define the feature-level KPIs and success metrics each AI product is judged on. From there you'll own adoption and quality analysis and, partnering closely with the Experimentation & Causal Inference lead, bring rigor to measuring non-deterministic, fast-iterating AI features where a classic A/B read is hard. You'll work amid a data foundation still being built, consuming governed sources rather than rebuilding them, and raising the bar as you go. As the AI analytics lead, you set the measurement direction and standards for the domain and develop the analysts who join as it scales.

Responsibilities:

  • Own instrumentation coverage for the AI pillar -define the events and properties each AI surface must emit, and drive them into the roadmap with PMs and engineering
  • Define feature-level KPIs and success metrics for Voice AI, Conversation AI, AI Employee, and Ask AI -what "working" and "adopted" mean, made explicit and trusted
  • Partner with the Experimentation & Causal Inference lead to design and read AI experiments, including measurement approaches for non-deterministic, fast-iterating systems
  • Separate real signal from instrumentation gaps, novelty effects, and data maturity in every read
  • Set the measurement direction and standards for the AI analytics domain -the canonical metrics and instrumentation contracts other teams build on -and mentor analysts as the pod grows
  • Translate findings into clear recommendations for AI PMs and influence the roadmap without owning it
  • Flag data gaps to Analytics Engineering and help shape the event taxonomy AI analytics depends on
  • Use AI tooling (Claude and similar) to move faster on exploration, documentation, and analysis

Requirements:

  • 7+ years in product analytics, data science, or applied statistics, with hands-on ownership of a product area's metrics end to end
  • Strong instrumentation instinct -you've defined event tracking/taxonomy and driven it into a product roadmap, not just consumed existing tables
  • Ability to define success metrics for a product from a standing start and get stakeholders to adopt them
  • Fluency partnering on experiments (A/B design, guardrails) and interpreting results honestly
  • Strong SQL and working proficiency in Python; comfort in a Snowflake + dbt environment
  • Comfort working amid imperfect, in-progress data -you consume governed sources and help raise the bar rather than rebuilding pipelines
  • Cross-functional influence -you shift PM priorities without direct authority in a fast-moving environment

Nice to Have:

  • Experience measuring AI/ML or LLM-based product features, including non-deterministic systems
  • B2B SaaS, CRM, or product-led growth background
  • Experience with conversational, voice, or agent/assistant products
  • Familiarity with Statsig or a comparable experimentation platform
  • Exposure to AI-assisted analytics workflows

Success in this role looks like:

  • The AI surfaces are instrumented to a standard that makes them measurable, with coverage gaps closed on a known schedule
  • Each AI product has agreed, trusted feature-level KPIs and success metrics everyone uses
  • Adoption and quality of AI features are understood by segment, not guessed at
  • AI experiments are designed and read rigorously despite non-deterministic behavior
  • AI PMs make roadmap calls off the analysis, and the pillar has a foundation the next analysts can build on

Datacor is the leading provider of software solutions, including ERP, CRM, Asset Tracking, Simulation and Formulation, to the process manufacturing space. We are on a mission to better equip the industry with software solutions and move it forward by building thoughtful, intuitive products that solve our customers’ most difficult problems.

Our customers make products that extend and sustain lives by sanitizing, fertilizing, beautifying, cleaning, and recycling the world we live in. We at Datacor help our customers make those products you use every day more safely, cost effectively and more efficiently through our technology platforms and applications.

About this role:

Feed mills and grain businesses run their daily operations on Datacor Animal Nutrition’s Feed ERP products, Feed Mill Manager and Pennent Mill Manager: commodity merchandising, procurement, plant production, and delivery. As Lead Product Manager, you own the strategy, roadmap, and revenue outcomes for this product line.

This role is not a backlog-management job. You are accountable for product-level ARR, net revenue retention, and win rate, and you set pricing and packaging direction. The core qualification is industry depth: you understand how merchandisers, plant managers, and feed businesses actually work, and you turn that into products they will pay for.

What you will do:

Strategy & Commercial Ownership

  • Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Feed Mill Manager and Pennent Mill Manager, aligning Engineering, Services, Support, and Commercial teams on priorities that drive retention, cross-sell, upsell, and new-market growth.

  • Own the numbers. Accountable for product-level ARR, net revenue retention, and win rate.

  • Build the pricing and packaging recommendation, including tier design and customer migration, and present it to the Datacor Pricing Committee.

  • Frame ambiguous business goals into a problem, options, and a plan. Make product-level tradeoffs, influence resourcing within the unit, and work across Datacor products to avoid duplicative investment.

Market & Customer Discovery

  • Run competitive research and win/loss analysis, and turn findings into roadmap and positioning changes.

  • Lead the product advisory group, from agenda to synthesis to follow-through, and represent Datacor Animal Nutrition at industry events.

  • Validate before you build. Set success criteria up front, test ideas with customers using AI-built prototypes, and kill work that misses the bar.

  • Own AI-enabled capabilities in the product, including quality bars, failure modes, and customer trust, and an AI-assisted discovery workflow that is fast and verifiable.

Delivery, Launch & Leadership

  • Prioritize the backlog against the roadmap, defining use cases, requirements, and measurable outcomes, and escalating cross-functional risks and blockers.

  • Own tiered launches with readiness gates and success criteria. Drive Sales, Services, and Support enablement (battlecards, objection handling, AE/SE readiness) and partner with Product Marketing on analyst briefings, webinars, and user conference sessions.

  • Lead without direct authority. Broker competing priorities, hold the line on product decisions, coach junior PMs, and own interview loops for the product.

What we are looking for

Required:

  • Feed industry depth. Meaningful experience in agribusiness, feed manufacturing, or commodity trading, with working knowledge of at least two of: commodity merchandising, ingredient procurement, feed plant operations or livestock feed regulatory requirements.

  • Product line ownership. You have owned a B2B software product’s roadmap and business outcomes, balancing strategy with delivery.

  • Commercial judgment. Evidence that your pricing, packaging, win/loss, or business case work changed a decision.

  • Discovery craft. You push past a customer’s requested solution to the underlying problem and validate before committing engineering time.

  • Strong communication. You can lay out a problem, options, tradeoffs, and a recommendation in a written narrative someone can act on without a meeting, and present it credibly to executives, engineers, and customers.

  • Hands-on AI use. You use AI daily to research, draft, analyze, and prototype, and you know when its output needs verification.

  • Technical fluency. Comfortable discussing data models, integrations, and product details with development teams.

  • Ownership without authority. You drive results through teams that do not report to you, and you travel to customers and events.

  • Education. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred:

  • Experience with feed and/or ration formulation software, familiarity with nutrition or feed labeling regulations, software development, or product managing AI or data-driven capabilities.

jobs.jd_full:
About The Company

goop is a lifestyle platform dedicated to exploration, curation, and groundbreaking conversation. From its award-winning beauty and fashion lines to its expansive editorial lens, goop invites women to embrace the process of becoming, and to discover deep joy in the pursuit of pleasure, beauty, and growth in all phases of life.

Gwyneth Paltrow began goop in the fall of 2008 as a weekly newsletter. It has expanded into a beauty, fashion, and food business that’s also known for its products, curation, podcast, TV shows, live events, and retail stores.

About You

You’re an executor. You take direction and turn it into action fast, with accuracy and follow-through. You live in Notion and Slack, you set up new tools with ease, and you run operations so smoothly that everyone knows what’s happening, who owns it and when it’s due.

You’re AI-native and use technology to make every workflow faster, simpler and more reliable.

Who You Are

  • Extremely executional: you get things done quickly and correctly, and you close every loop
  • Strong operational manager: you run the machine behind the business, including calendars, logistics, tools, vendors, budgets and follow-through
  • Systems builder: you learn new tools fast, set them up right the first time, and get people using them
  • Highly organized: you manage a high volume of parallel projects without dropping a thread
  • Skilled researcher: you gather information quickly and present it clearly
  • Thoughtful communicator, verbally and in writing: you’re polished, considered and concise, you read the room, and you know how to communicate with a founder. Your updates, to-dos and summaries are clear, specific and easy to act on
  • Collaborative, with a good sense of humor: you stay steady and easy to work with under pressure
  • Trustworthy and discreet: you handle sensitive information with care

How You Operate

  •   You communicate early and often; proactive updates are your default
  •   You follow direction closely and ask the right questions when something is unclear
  •   You’re warm and direct
  •   You understand that small details, done right, build long-term trust

About the Role

This role reports directly to goop’s Founder & Co-CEO and is dedicated to the Founder’s business. You’ll work in close partnership with Co-CEO Moj Mahdara and the executive team, and you’ll be a trusted, day-to-day point of contact for the Founder. Strategy and decisions are set by the two Co-CEOs; your job is to execute. You coordinate the projects and needs coming from both Co-CEOs and the executive team, and you make sure every action item is tracked, assigned and completed.

Your number one responsibility is running the Notion calendar and logistics. You also set up and roll out the tools and systems the team relies on, and you manage a pipeline of research and trend reports.

CALENDAR & LOGISTICS MANAGEMENT

  • Own the Notion calendar as the central view of meetings, travel, launches, partner deliverables and deadlines
  • Work closely with the Founder’s Executive Assistant(s) on scheduling holds, availability and logistics for projects, events and partner commitments

  • Produce executive dinners and events from start to finish: guest lists, invitations, RSVPs and follow-ups, vendors, menus, gifting, budgets and on-site coordination
  • Flag calendar conflicts, gaps and upcoming deadlines weeks ahead

PROJECT MANAGEMENT & EXECUTION

  • Execute projects led by the Co-CEOs: build the project plan in Notion, track milestones and owners, and drive every task to completion
  • Capture action items from executive meetings and make sure every one is tracked, assigned and closed
  • Keep a live view of all active projects showing what’s in progress, what’s at risk and what’s blocked, and flag issues to the Co-CEOs early
  • Follow up with senior leaders and teams to keep deliverables on schedule
  • Coordinate with the podcast production team and the Co-CEOs on the guest tracker, booking follow-ups, scheduling and production sign-offs
  • Route materials through the approval workflows set by the Co-CEOs, so items reach the Founder ready for review
  • Keep a master budget and vendor tracker for each project, including payment status and anything outstanding
  • Keep a current library of approved assets (bio, headshots, boilerplate, brand guidelines) so teams and partners always get the latest version

STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS DELIVERY

  • Project manage brand partnership deliverables once agreements are signed: timelines, assets, approvals and deadlines
  • Organize partner kickoff calls and keep a deliverables plan with owners, dates and approval status
  • Coordinate across internal teams and partner teams so deliverables ship on time and to spec
  • Keep partnership work-streams visible in Notion and Slack so the Co-CEOs always know their status

TOOLS & SYSTEMS SETUP

  • Set up new tools and AI apps selected by the Co-CEOs for the Founder and the executive team, including configuration, accounts, permissions and integrations
  • Onboard the Founder and executives into new systems with short training, simple guides and follow-up support until the tools are in daily use
  • Carry out tool migrations and consolidations (for example email platforms, inboxes and task systems) with minimal disruption
  • Connect tools so work flows between them automatically, for example meeting notes to Notion tasks, and Slack requests to tracked to-dos
  • Coordinate outside developers, consultants and IT partners working on systems, and keep their work on schedule
  • Work with IT and security to confirm new tools meet access and data-security standards before rollout

SLACK, NOTION & WORKSPACE MANAGEMENT

  • Organize projects in Slack using canvases, lists, pinned files and links, so every project has one clear home
  • Set up automated updates, summaries and reminders in Slack and Notion so the Co-CEOs and executive team get visibility without extra meetings
  • Build and maintain Notion databases, dashboards and templates for projects, to-dos and follow-ups
  • Administer the Slack and WhatsApp workspaces and keep them clean: channel and group structure, naming conventions, permissions, archiving and consistent project setup
  • Keep contact records and trackers accurate, deduplicated and consistently structured

RESEARCH & TREND REPORTS

  • Manage a pipeline of research requests from the Co-CEOs: log each request, track progress in Notion and deliver on deadline
  • Research and compile trend reports across wellness, beauty, fashion, consumer, culture and AI, following the briefs set by the Co-CEOs
  • Run quick research on companies, categories and markets as requests come in, and deliver clear, well-sourced summaries
  • Maintain a tagged, searchable research and trend library in Notion
  • Use AI research tools and agents to scan sources, summarize findings and track emerging signals

LOCATION, TRAVEL & HOURS

  • This is a remote role. You must be based in a North American time zone
  • You’ll travel 8–10 times a year, for meetings, events and time with the team
  • You work on the Founder’s schedule and are available during her working hours, including early mornings or late evenings when needed
  • Core hours align with Pacific or Eastern Time. The Founder travels regularly across time zones, so occasional flexibility is needed for time-sensitive travel, events and deadlines

Qualifications & Experience

  • Experience: 3–5 years of business experience, including at least 2 years in project management or executive operations supporting C-level leaders. Consumer goods or brand partnership experience strongly preferred.
  • Technical skills: Expert in Notion (calendars, databases, dashboards, templates, automations). Administrator-level experience with Slack (workspace setup, permissions, canvases, lists, workflows, channel management) and WhatsApp (business accounts, groups, access and security settings). Advanced user of Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini, and of Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides). Hands-on experience building workflows, AI agents and automations that connect these tools (e.g., Zapier, Notion automations, Slack workflows).
  • Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business required.
  • Skills: Exceptional written and verbal communication, with experience communicating directly with a founder or CEO. Exceptional organization, speed and follow-through, and experience working across time zones with global, cross-functional teams.
  • Based in North America and able to travel 8–10 times a year.

FAQ

The Opportunity

GPC builds ServiceNow’s AI-native partner ecosystem across five Routes to Market: Hyperscaler, ISV/Build, Resell, Service Provider, and Consulting & Implementation. Partners deliver approximately 90% of every ServiceNow deployment and source a growing share of the company’s new business making the GPC narrative one of the most consequential stories the company tells.

The Office of GPC drives the organization’s rhythm of business, shapes how GPC’s story lands with our CEO, Board, and partner C-suites, and turns partner strategy into artifacts that ship. Executive Materials (~30%)

Rhythm of Business (~25%)

Reporting & Partner Intelligence (~15%)

  • Build the support analysis that shows leaders where the ecosystem is working and where it is not
